from.place: the pro-system Hom computation in the proof of the pre-derived adjunction

title: Hom out of an essentially constant pro-system value is the colimit of Hom sets
statement: Let $J$ be a cofiltered category, $\mathcal C$ a category, and $G:J\to\mathcal C$ a diagram that is essentially constant as a pro-object with value $X$ in the sense of [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram] (Stacks, Categories, Definition Tag 05PU(2)), with cone maps $u_j:X\to G(j)$. For every object $Y$ of $\mathcal C$, the canonical map $\varinjlim_{j\in J}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(G(j),Y)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal C}(X,Y)$ induced by the cone maps $u_j$ is a bijection.

source.place: Stacks Tag 0FND, label lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general, proof line 9515, sixth equality; Categories Tag 05PZ, label categories-lemma-characterize-essentially-constant-pro

proof.text: By Stacks Definition Tag 05PU(2), choose the cone maps $u_j:X\to G(j)$, an index $j_0$ and $r:G(j_0)\to X$ with $r\circ u_{j_0}=\operatorname{id}_X$; for every transition $a:j'\to j$, $u_j=G(a)\circ u_{j'}$. Define $[f:G(j)\to Y]\mapsto f\circ u_j$. Since $(f\circ G(a))\circ u_{j'}=f\circ u_j$, this is independent of the representative in the colimit (filtered, as $J$ is cofiltered).

source.place: Categories, Definition Tag 05PU (label categories-definition-essentially-constant-diagram), part (2); Lemma Tag 05PZ

proof.text: For $h:X\to Y$, take the representative $h\circ r:G(j_0)\to Y$. Its image is $(h\circ r)\circ u_{j_0}=h\circ(r\circ u_{j_0})=h$, so every morphism $X\to Y$ lies in the image.

source.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PZ, condition (4) and the surjectivity calculation

proof.text: If $f:G(j)\to Y$ and $g:G(k)\to Y$ satisfy $f\circ u_j=g\circ u_k$, choose by cofilteredness $l$ with transitions $a:l\to j$ and $b:l\to k$. By the factorization clause of Stacks Definition Tag 05PU(2) applied to $l$, there are $m$ and transitions $c:m\to l$, $d:m\to j_0$ with $G(c)=u_l\circ r\circ G(d)$. Then $f\circ G(a)\circ G(c)=f\circ G(a)\circ u_l\circ r\circ G(d)=f\circ u_j\circ r\circ G(d)=g\circ u_k\circ r\circ G(d)=g\circ G(b)\circ G(c)$, so the two representatives agree at $m$ and define the same class in the filtered colimit, proving injectivity.

proof_origin.place: Categories, Lemma Tag 05PZ, implication (1) to (4), specialized to the Hom-colimit conclusion
